title: Name a created session's initial window after the session; --window-name overrides or disables
Explore driving remote tmux targets from the embedded launcher
notes:
Design handoff: /design/launcher/remote0.glm53max.md (2026-10-27, ses_e818d4b00ffe1ewolZWtBj7BsP).

Motivated by term-preserver's default embedded backend exposing the asymmetry: remote transports exec whatever tta binary the host carries, and a stale remote tta 0.1.0 rejecting the carrier's --scaffold flag broke remote launching in the wild.

The doc lays out four unprescribed directions (remote-exec transport, forwarded control socket, remote worker protocol, structured carrier), five constraints (terminal locality, mosh exec channel, socket auth, cold start, scaffold filesystem), and candidate structuring in a per-state host-annotated launch state machine plus trait seams. First coherent slice: pick or combine directions, likely starting from the open questions list.

title: Give each terminal an independent workspace view with safe invoking-client targeting
description: Human clarification on 2026-10-23 in parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5: different tta-entered terminals must independently choose their current window while sharing the project windows/processes; advance tmax switching and attachment preparation where sound. Current default plain tta attaches all terminals to one session and therefore shares current-window selection. Explicit --group correctly gives separate grouped sessions with shared panes. Investigation in opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea reproduced a separate inside-switch defect using two real PTYs on pinned tmux 3.7c: after terminal A starts a delayed tta other from a shared pane, more recent activity from B causes the CLI switch to move B instead. Both inputs have identical TMUX, TMUX_PANE and pane tty; a subprocess cannot uniquely recover which attached client supplied its input. Source confirms activity-based current-client selection. Native querying of client_name alone would freeze that heuristic, not prove origin. Need a deliberate target contract before claiming robust native switching. Recommended direction: independent grouped views by default, retain --group=false for intentionally shared selection, explicit authoritative client context supplied by a tmux binding/integration, safe auto-resolution only when provably unique, refuse ambiguity rather than moving an unrelated terminal. This remains a proposal at the requested architectural checkpoint, not an implemented default or new knob.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decide and record client-origin contract and ambiguous shared-pane behavior. 2) Normal entry gives two real terminals separate current-window selection over shared windows/panes; document old shared behavior opt-out. 3) Repeated same-project inside calls reuse the current independent view where identifiable; entering another project targets exactly the invoking client. 4) Cover cold first entry, second entry, shared-pane ambiguity, existing groups/base loss/canonical matching, concurrent entrants and detach/last-view lifecycle. 5) Advance native switching/attachment preparation only with explicit target and lifecycle safety; preserve print-shell observation-only equivalence, literal argv/cwd/scaffold/endpoint contracts and no blind mutation retry. Keep interactive terminal UI on real tmux unless a separately authorized implementation exists.
notes:
Architectural checkpoint reached, not a completed default/native-switch implementation. Evidence committed in tta 9380e3c5; tmax consumer account in d8bf376d. Pointers: design/launcher/launch-backends1.gpt61sol.md; verification/trials/independent-views/README.md, proof.py, native0.json and cli0.json. Main guide now states current shared default and warns about the inside-switch defect. The preserved trial executes the real tta in TWO REAL PTYs on exclusively owned /tmp/opencode sockets, using version-asserted local tmux 3.7c. Four cases (plain/grouped x native/CLI) reproduced: default terminals share a current window; --group gives separate sessions with shared panes and independent windows. With both views showing the same pane, A enters delayed tta other and B becomes active; B is switched instead of A on both backend selections. Recorded actual native A PID 3345281 -> switched B PID 3345375; CLI A PID 3345285 -> switched B PID 3345373. Identical TMUX/TMUX_PANE/pane tty and tmux source prove that normal shared-pane subprocess context lacks authoritative input-origin identity; a native query of client_name only freezes the recent-activity heuristic. Existing single-client acceptance/launch suites still pass 24/24, exposing the coverage gap. Combined CLI build, generated JSON parsing and rkt documentation/provenance checks pass. No Rust production code/default/API version changed.
Decision needed: (1, recommended) make grouped views default, retain --group=false, add authoritative client-context input/integration from a tmux-owned boundary, native switch-client -c and refuse ambiguity; (2) explicitly accept tmux recent-activity heuristics as a weaker contract; or (3) deliver default independent outside entry separately while leaving the known inside CLI defect pending. Do not silently choose a new knob/integration/error contract. Native attachment still needs real terminal client exec. Native queue compositions remain candidates to test: inside create/switch-explicit-client/keep-last in one queue; outside native create plus satellite-local temporary destroy-unattached=off in one queue, then CLI attach/keep-last. No queue workaround was claimed safe or implemented. Parent/user choice is prerequisite to the next coherent implementation slice. Session opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea; parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5.

title: Backend-selectable launch execution: native tmax mutations with tmux-client terminal handoff
description:
Origin: user ask "do we use ~/src/tmax or are we shelling out? i'd love a build feature that switches between the two. tempted to make tmax the default." The parent audit (opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5, commits dd4d7806/ea852864/9bcb6354) satisfied the LOOKUP half and closed tta-lookup-backends; this ticket holds the remainder so the board shows launch/backend execution still open. It does not claim the closed audit finished native launch.

What exists today (verified by reading current code, opencode://ses_e9a5990dfffeEYjKIU71KHzxZo):
- Lookup alone is backend-selectable. session/launcher/src/backend.rs: Native queries the tmax endpoint directly; Cli runs the same typed Sessions query through a tmux subprocess. app/cli/src/main.rs selects native/cli via Cargo features plus --backend / TTA_BACKEND (CLI > env > native-if-compiled), native default.
- ALL launch mutations and terminal handoff are planned as tmux argv. session/launcher/src/plan.rs builds tta_command Expressions over tmax operation::Invocations (new-session, attach-session, switch-client, set-option destroy-unattached); shell/command executes or renders them; app/cli/src/main.rs execs the tmux client (Handoff::Exec) or renders for eval (--print-shell / --exec-shell).
- Operation matrix (main.rs trace names): existing -> attach-session | switch-client; project -> new-session+attach | new-session-detached+switch-client; create -> scaffold+new-session(+attach | +switch); grouped -> new-grouped-session-detached+attach | +switch-client (detached create, set-option, then client move).

Closed-audit scope (tta-lookup-backends): verified feature selection and native default for session discovery only; fixed 3 scaffold tests that hardcoded the cli backend in native-only builds; documented the boundary in README.md#build-and-install (22/22 native-only, 20/20 cli-only+scaffold, 32/32 combined CLI+PTY). Closure = lookup verification, not native launch.

Remaining outcome: a deliberate backend selection for launch EXECUTION (mutations and handoff), preserving interactive terminal attachment through the real tmux client and unchanged --print-shell emission.

Verified tmax capabilities (~/src/tmax -> ~/src/tmux-interface-control; README and src read this session):
- Native mutation execution exists: endpoint::Tmux::run accepts impl IntoInvocation, implemented for raw operation::Invocation; plan.rs already assembles Invocations with argv boundaries preserved, and typed builders (e.g. NewSession) also run natively.
- Endpoints never spawn a client or start a server. An absent server surfaces as OperationError::ServerConnection; backend.rs already maps NotFound/ConnectionRefused to an empty inventory for lookup.
- Cold server: opt-in server-lifecycle OwnedServer launches `tmux -D` in the foreground at a FRESH explicit socket under a supervisor — private-server ownership, not shared-socket auto-start. Today's CLI plan relies on the exec'd tmux client auto-starting the server; a native create on an absent server fails instead. Cold-start posture is an open decision.
- No interactive terminal client exists in tmax: the process-launching root Tmux was removed, and the persistent Session's control-mode attach is a control client, not a terminal UI. attach-session handoff must remain an exec'd tmux client.

Open questions needing design resolution (design-first is acceptable; do not pre-decide):
- switch-client scope: the CLI command mutates the INVOKING client (tta detects its own context via socket.rs client_mode/$TMUX). A native control connection is a different client; how or whether the user's terminal client can be switched from a control connection is unresolved.
- Atomicity: the grouped flow currently creates + switches + sets destroy-unattached in ONE tmux invocation; splitting mutations (native) from handoff (exec) opens a partial-failure window needing explicit recovery semantics.
- Client-flag mapping: -f config, TMUX_TMPDIR, -L/-S live on the tmux client invocation in the plan; native execution maps the socket via Tmux::new().socket_path/socket_name (socket::Resolved already carries it), but startup-config semantics at server start need a decision.
- Cold-server posture (above) and whether native becomes the default for mutations as it already is for lookup (user leans tmax default).

Coherent possible scope, offered not decided: mirror the SessionLookup seam with a launch-execution seam in session/launcher — plan.rs stays pure assembly; an execution backend chooses native Tmux::run for mutations versus Expression exec, keeping print-shell rendering and terminal handoff on the Expression path.

Implementation homes: session/launcher/src/plan.rs (assembly), session/launcher/src/backend.rs (lookup seam to mirror), shell/command/src/lib.rs (Expression execute/shell), app/cli/src/main.rs (selection, handoff, print-shell), session/launcher/src/socket.rs (socket/client-mode context), README.md#build-and-install.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design resolved and recorded: backend granularity (Cargo feature vs runtime flag), cold-server posture on absent server, switch-client scope from a control connection, partial-failure semantics for split mutate+handoff, and -f config mapping. 2) A launch-execution seam exists beside SessionLookup with mutation operations runnable natively (Tmux::run over the Invocations plan.rs already builds) and via the CLI path, selected per the decided granularity. 3) Interactive attach/switch terminal handoff still execs the real tmux client; --print-shell/--exec-shell output is unchanged for both selections. 4) Feature-matrix verification on tmux 3.7c: existing/project/create/grouped flows on each backend plus mixed selection, cold-server behavior matching the decided posture, and PTY acceptance coverage mirroring the closed audit's configurations.
notes:
Context ticket written by opencode://ses_e9a5990dfffeEYjKIU71KHzxZo (G subagent) on direction from parent audit opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5, which closed tta-lookup-backends as lookup-only. Capability claims verified against ~/src/tmux-interface-control README.md, src/endpoint/mod.rs (run/query signatures), src/server/mod.rs (OwnedServer), src/lib.rs docs, and tta's current backend.rs/plan.rs/main.rs/shell-command. No implementation done here; keep open until the design questions are resolved and an execution seam lands.
Implementation scope selected in opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea (parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5): take the straight native slice, grouped satellite detached creation only. Keep attach/switch followed by keep-last in one real tmux-client invocation, preserving invoking-client selection, option timing and terminal ownership. Ordinary project/create launches retain CLI creation, cold-start/config behavior and raw Unix startup argv. Add a reusable prepared launch with native/CLI execution selection while preserving the existing launch()->Expression API and unchanged print-shell output. Native errors stop without retry/rollback. Ticket remains open for broader native project creation and switching; no full interactive client or new server supervisor is authorized.
Completed the bounded native-default improvement in opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea (parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5): tta commit 86f9d87c after preparatory checkpoint a900ac90; tmax commit f7fb3acdf6aba8df72d5f4f2a56eb1816bcf7b69. FINAL SCOPE SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER SATELLITE-SPLIT NOTE: grouped create -> attach/switch -> keep-last stays one CLI queue, because splitting native detached creation allows inherited destroy-unattached to remove the satellite before attachment. Native now creates ordinary project/scaffold sessions detached INSIDE a live selected server when startup argv is UTF-8, then retains exact-target CLI switching of the invoking client. Current pointers: README.md#which-operations-use-tmax; design/launcher/launch-backends0.gpt61sol.md (decision, failure policy, rejected split, verification); session/launcher/src/execution.rs; app/cli/tests/launch.rs; library-side /home/rektide/src/tmux-interface-control/doc/consumer/tta.md.
Verification: system tmux was discovered to be 3.8, so built and version-asserted a private 3.7c binary from the local archive tag and repeated the full feature matrix with it first on PATH. Pinned 3.7c workspace nextest: default native+scaffold 110/110, CLI-only 84/84, combined 122/122. System 3.8 also passed 110/84/122 configurations, and CLI-only with explicit scaffold features passed 24/24 focused CLI/launch/scaffold/PTY checks. Combined and CLI-only clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings passed; formatting and workspace doctests passed; rkt OKF/link/provenance checks passed. Library isolated endpoint tests 6/6 and streams locked offline compile passed. Adjacent tmax materialize compile remains blocked by its existing unhandled Kubeless PublicationReport::Enqueued; only receiving locks were refreshed, no unrelated materialize implementation changed. All sockets private under /tmp/opencode.
Ticket deliberately remains OPEN for broader native switch-client identity, queue-preserving grouped mutation and raw-byte startup capabilities; this is not a full native terminal client or all-launch migration. The user-authorized straightforward default-native creation slice is complete.
2026-10-23 human clarified the primary outcome: each tta-entered terminal independently chooses its window over shared project windows/processes, while advancing native tmax switching/attachment preparation. Added linked child tta-launch-backends-independent-views (blocked at explicit user/parent targeting-contract choice). Investigation/evidence in tta 9380e3c5 and tmax consumer-account commit d8bf376d. Pointers: design/launcher/launch-backends1.gpt61sol.md and verification/trials/independent-views/README.md. Two real PTYs on pinned tmux 3.7c confirm grouping provides exactly the requested window independence, whereas plain current default shares the session selection. Also reproduced an existing wrong-client switch on BOTH backend selections: A invokes delayed tta other, B becomes active, and B moves instead. Shared-pane TMUX, TMUX_PANE and tty are identical; client_name lookup does not prove origin. This is already a CLI defect, so merely native-switching its inferred client would not be robust. Existing acceptance/launch tests remain green 24/24; the preserved four-case trial exposes the uncovered ambiguity. Recommended next contract: grouped default with --group=false escape, authoritative client context from a boundary that knows the actual tmux client, explicit native -c targeting and ambiguity refusal. Parent should select that versus deliberately accepting weaker activity heuristics or splitting outside-default delivery first. No new production defaults/native-switch APIs were silently implemented. Broader ticket remains OPEN; real interactive attachment still requires tmux client exec. Native grouped preparation/queue options are recorded as unverified candidates, not dismissed as fundamentally impossible or claimed implemented. title: Skeleton-generation mode: scaffold missing projects before creating the session
notes:
Commissioned and v1 implemented in session opencode://ses_e9b671d21ffeJXXTDi6GZnjm60 (lucky-moon).

Decisions recorded 2026-10-22:
- Trigger: unambiguous miss only (no session, no immediate directory under root, no candidates). Ambiguity still stops; existing sessions still win.
- Adapter crates: each scaffolding system is its own crate under scaffold/ behind app/cli cargo features. v1: scaffold/rekon wraps the external rekon script (program rekon, one arg: project name, PATH lookup). Native Rust port of the script is a deliberate later step ('not so crappy'); caveat: the script hardcodes ~/src so a non-default TTA_ROOT diverges until the port.
- Registry: named registry in a TOML config file (~/.config/tta/config.toml, TTA_CONFIG overrides). Entries [scaffold.generators.NAME] with adapter = compiled adapter name; [scaffold] default picks the miss generator. Empty/absent registry keeps today's miss error.
- Posture: default create-on-miss via default feature scaffold-by-default; removing the feature flips the default to opt-in. Per-invocation: --scaffold[=NAME] / --scaffold=false and TTA_SCAFFOLD env, CLI > env > compiled default.
- Safety: fragment must be a safe single path component; session-name validation and collision checks run before the generator executes; refuse if root/NAME already exists; plan is generator && cd -P && tmux new-session, short-circuiting.
- Design doc: design/scaffold/proposal0.glm53max.md
v1 implemented and verified in session opencode://ses_e9b671d21ffeJXXTDi6GZnjm60, commits 'Add scaffold adapter crate and create-mode resolution and planning', 'Add TOML scaffold registry, config loading, and CLI scaffold mode', 'Document scaffold mode and record the design decisions'.
